rationale: A %TAG directive declares a HANDLE, and a tag that uses it resolves THROUGH that declaration. This is the third of the four tag forms and the only one a document-model parser and a syntax parser both have to reason about to agree. The shape-safety gate found the gap rather than a review: `tag_directive` was named by the analyzer and present in the grammar, and no fixture exercised it, so the branch was unproven -- which is the F3 rule catching a lane that had renamed and re-typed every tag but had never run a %TAG directive. Pinned: the handle lands in metadata, `!e!thing` expands to `tag:example.com,2000:thing`, and all three forms (local `!!`, handle, verbatim `!<...>`) produce a declared_type edge.
